rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and glad Halcyon Threshold came up. I'm going to pass on an attributed quote for now — I'm not doing named press at the moment. Nothing personal about the piece. If it's useful on background: Halcyon Threshold is a small, early-stage effort to help make the arrival of very capable AI go well, focused on neglected, concrete work rather than taking sides in a doomers-vs-builders framing. Happy to reconnect for a future piece once we have public work to point to. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter: politely declined the named quote (your no-press rule), left the door open.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing in this round — as a matter of policy we're not adding our name to published sign-on letters at this stage of the organization. Please do keep us on your list for future governance work; I'd be glad to stay in touch with Tomasz and the team. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter: declined the sign-on (names go to press), kept the relationship warm.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes please, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that means a lot, and yes, there's something concrete that fits a data analyst at ~5 hours/week. The project: a \"commitments tracker.\" Frontier AI labs and governments have published a growing pile of safety commitments (frontier safety frameworks, responsible scaling policies, summit pledges, eval/reporting promises). Nobody systematically tracks what was promised, by whom, with what trigger conditions, and whether it's being kept. That's measurable, neglected, and exactly the kind of accountability infrastructure that helps the transition to very capable AI go well. A useful first pass, entirely at your own pace: 1. A spreadsheet of public commitments: source org, date, exact quoted commitment, trigger/threshold if any, verifiable? (y/n), status (kept / pending / broken / unverifiable), link to source. 2. Start with the major labs' published safety frameworks and the 2023–2025 summit-style pledges — even 20–30 well-sourced rows would be a real foundation. Strict rule for this dataset: public, citable sources only — no private or off-the-record information. If that sounds good, just start and send me whatever format you like; we'll iterate. And if a different angle excites you more, tell me — the help is the valuable part. Thanks again, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: accepted her offer, gave her the tracker's initial data-collection task (public sources only) — replied by email.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly ops" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: weekly Monday 9am ops session scheduled with your constraints baked into its instructions.
